title: If Paradise is only for you, why fear death?
subtitle: A claim tested against the heart

row.title: how you feel about meeting Him

then: Some claimed the home of the Hereafter was theirs alone. The Prophet ﷺ was told to answer: {idea}then wish for death, if you are truthful.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said it meant: call on Allah to bring death on whichever side is lying. {trap}They declined.{/trap}
now: It is easy to say I am fine with Allah in a discussion at the dinner table. The honest check is quieter. When you think of meeting Him tonight, do you feel ready, or do you want more time to fix things? {idea}That feeling tells you what to work on.{/idea}
old: I am sure I am on the right side, so I have nothing to worry about.
new: My real confidence shows in how I feel about meeting Allah, not in what I claim.
try: Ask yourself honestly: if I met Allah tonight, what would I want to have fixed? Start on it.

title: They will never wish it, because of what their hands sent ahead.
subtitle: Deeds go ahead of us
then: The verse answers its own challenge. {trap}They will never wish for death, because of what their hands have sent before them.{/trap} Ibn Kathir: because they knew the Prophet ﷺ was true, yet denied him. {idea}Allah knows the wrongdoers.{/idea}
now: Every message you send, every shift you work honestly or not, every kindness at home goes ahead of you like luggage on a flight. {idea}You will meet it at the other end.{/idea} The good news: you can still add to what goes ahead today.
old: What I did is in the past, it is behind me.
new: What I did has gone ahead of me, and I will meet it again.
try: Send one good deed ahead today on purpose: a charity, a visit, a sincere apology.

title: A thousand years would not move him one step from it.
subtitle: A long life is not an escape

row.title: only what I do with it

then: The verse describes {trap}people greedier for life than anyone, wishing to live a thousand years.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said long life would not save them from punishment. Ibn Zayd compared it to Iblis, whose long life did not help him. {idea}Allah sees what they do.{/idea}
now: The anti-ageing creams. The fear of birthdays. The plan to turn to Allah when you retire. {trap}Time alone fixes nothing.{/trap} {reward}A short life spent well is worth more than a long one spent running.{/reward}
old: If I just have more years, I will sort myself out.
new: More years only help if I change. Changing can start today.
try: Pick one change you are postponing until later in life. Do a small piece of it this week.

title: Enemy of Jibril? He only brought what Allah sent.
subtitle: Blaming the messenger for the message
then: Ibn Jarir said scholars agree this was revealed when some said {trap}Jibril is our enemy, Mikail our friend.{/trap} Anas narrated that Abdullah bin Salam heard the Prophet ﷺ say Jibril told him the answers to three questions, then accepted Islam. {idea}Jibril brings nothing except by Allah's command.{/idea}
now: You do not like the imam, so you ignore the reminder he gave. You do not like your sister in law, so the true thing she said does not count. {trap}Disliking the carrier is an easy way out of the message.{/trap}
old: I cannot take that seriously, look who said it.
new: If the message is from Allah, my feelings about the carrier do not change it.
try: Think of a good reminder you dismissed because of who said it. Take one thing from it today.

title: You cannot pick and choose among Allah's angels and messengers.
subtitle: Enmity to one is enmity to all

row.title: I can love one and hate another

then: Jibril and Mikail are both named because some claimed one as enemy and the other as friend. Ibn Kathir: {idea}whoever takes one messenger as an enemy has taken them all as enemies,{/idea} since all are sent by Allah. He cites 22:75: Allah chooses messengers from angels and from people.
now: You love the verses about mercy and skip the ones about accountability. You quote one scholar you like and wave off another who is just as sound. {idea}Guidance comes as a whole.{/idea} Taking only the parts you like is choosing yourself over the Sender.
old: I accept the parts of the message that feel right to me.
new: The angels and messengers all serve one Lord. Accepting Him means accepting all of them.
try: Read one verse today on a topic you usually avoid. Sit with it without arguing.

title: The signs are clear. Only defiance denies them.
subtitle: When the problem is not the evidence
then: Ibn Jarir said the clear signs included the Quran telling the hidden details of earlier scriptures. Ibn Abbas: {idea}you recite this Book though you never read a book, and you tell them what is in theirs.{/idea} The verse says {trap}only the defiantly disobedient deny such signs.{/trap}
now: You ask for one more sign before you change. Then it comes, a scare at the clinic, a friend's sudden death, and you ask for another. {trap}At some point the question is not proof but will.{/trap}
old: If I had clearer proof, I would commit.
new: The signs are already clear. What I need is the will to act on them.
try: Name one sign Allah has already shown you. Act on it in one small way today.

title: Every promise made, some threw it away.
subtitle: A pattern of broken pledges
then: When reminded of their covenant about the Prophet ﷺ, Malik bin As-Sayf said Allah never took any pledge from them. Then this verse came. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: {trap}they make a promise today and break it tomorrow.{/trap}
now: I will start praying properly after Eid. I will call my father this weekend. I will stop that habit from Monday. {trap}A promise you keep breaking becomes a pattern.{/trap} {idea}Small promises kept build a trustworthy heart.{/idea}
old: I meant it when I promised. Breaking it later is just life.
new: The promises I keep breaking say something about what I really believe.
try: Keep one small promise today, even one you made only to yourself.

title: The Book thrown behind their backs, as if unknown.
subtitle: Turning away from what you know

row.title: as if they did not know

then: As-Suddi said: when the Prophet ﷺ came, they wanted to argue using the Torah, but {idea}the Torah and the Quran agreed.{/idea} So they set the Torah aside and turned to books of magic. Qatadah: {trap}they knew the truth, abandoned it, and denied even having it.{/trap}
now: The Quran on your shelf, wrapped in cloth, high and safe, and untouched since Ramadan. Not rejected. Just behind your back. {idea}Bring it in front of you again, even for one page.{/idea}
old: I respect the Quran, I just do not have time to read it.
new: Keeping the Book out of sight is a quiet way of throwing it behind my back.
try: Take the Quran down today and read one page, with the translation if you need it.

title: They swapped the Book for magic that harms and never helps.
subtitle: Sulayman was innocent; the devils were not
then: As-Suddi narrated that devils mixed lies with stolen news and spread books of sorcery, then claimed {trap}Sulayman ruled by magic.{/trap} The verse clears him: {idea}Sulayman did not disbelieve, the devils did.{/idea} The two angels at Babylon warned anyone first: we are a trial, do not disbelieve.
now: Someone suggests a person who can fix your marriage or bind a rival. Or you spend nights on videos about curses and charms. {trap}It promises control and delivers fear.{/trap} {idea}Nothing harms you except by Allah's leave.{/idea}
old: There must be some hidden power that can fix this for me.
new: No one can harm me except by Allah's leave, so I turn to Him, not to secrets.
try: When you feel afraid of harm from others, make a sincere dua for protection and leave it with Allah.

title: Had they believed and been mindful, the reward was far better.
subtitle: The door that stayed open
then: After the warning about magic, the verse turns gently. {reward}If they had believed and feared Allah, the reward from Him would have been better,{/reward} if only they knew. {idea}The better trade was always available.{/idea}
now: The shortcut always looks faster: the bribe to speed up the papers, the charm to win the person, the lie to close the sale. {reward}The slow way with Allah pays more, and it is never too late to take it.{/reward}
old: Doing it the straight way means losing out.
new: What Allah gives for faith and mindfulness is better than any shortcut.
try: Choose the straight way in one situation today where a shortcut tempts you.

title: Drop the word that can be twisted. Use a clear one.
subtitle: Manners of speech with the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: Ra'ina
sub: could be twisted into an insult

row.title: Unzurna
sub: look at us, help us understand

row.title: choose words that cannot be bent

then: Some used the word {trap}ra'ina with a twist of the tongue as mockery,{/trap} as 4:46 describes. Some believers used it innocently. Allah told the believers to {idea}say unzurna instead, a clear word with no double meaning, and to listen.{/idea}
now: A joke in the family group chat with a hidden edge. A reply at work that sounds polite but stings. Or an innocent word you keep using that others hear as mockery. {idea}Respectful speech chooses words that cannot be bent.{/idea}
old: My words are fine as long as I mean them well.
new: Good manners include choosing words that cannot be twisted into disrespect.
try: Before you send your next message, reread it once for any double meaning.

title: Some do not want good to reach you. Allah chooses anyway.
subtitle: Mercy is not up for others' approval

row.title: what Allah wills
sub: His mercy to whom He chooses

then: The verse tells the early believers that some among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters {trap}did not want any good sent down to them from their Lord.{/trap} The answer: {idea}Allah chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and He is the owner of great bounty.{/idea}
now: The relative who hopes your business fails. The colleague who would rather you did not get the role. You feel their wish like a weight. {idea}Their wish has no say in Allah's mercy.{/idea} Keep doing good and leave the giving to Him.
old: If they are against me, my chances are ruined.
new: No one's ill wish can stop the mercy Allah has chosen for me.
try: When you notice someone's envy, make dua for yourself and for them, and carry on.
